messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: kv-cache pressure + continuous-batching latency cliff detected on prod-usw2 cluster. 90th/99th tokens spiking, backend kv evictions rising sharply. auto-pager triggered :rotating_light:

eric: I'm on pager. can someone share the first visible symptom?

maria: saw a sudden jump in kv-store size and continuous-batch queue depth after the NTK long-context rollout at ~03:10 UTC. sampling shows lots of 1.2M token prefix keys hitting cache insertions.

sasha: confirming. metrics: kv_insert_rate x8, kv_eviction_rate x6, avg batch_size up from 6 -> 22 for longctx routes. tail latency for generation requests (1024+ ctx) jumped 2.7x.

eric: customer impact? any user-facing errors or 5xx?

maria: some customers on dedicated pools saw elevated 500s when the KV backend started OOMing on one node, but most traffic fell back to slower model variants — increased latency only for a subset using sliding-window prefetch + YaRN.

eric: ok. first actions: (1) throttle continuous-batching for longctx routes, (2) disable sliding-window prefetch for heavy customers, (3) put NTK rollout on pause. anyone can execute hotfix?

kai: I can patch routing rules. recommend immediate rollback of the NTK longctx knob that increased prefix caching aggressiveness. Also drop batch_window from 200ms -> 40ms for longctx routes.

sasha: agree. we should also pin those customers to smaller-model-quantized fallback to avoid kv churn.

devops-bot: Suggested commands:
```
# reduce continuous batching window (example)
redwoodctl set route --route longctx --batch_window 40ms
# disable sliding-window prefetch for specific customers
redwoodctl route update --customer CUST-123 --sliding_window false
# rollback NTK param
redwoodctl feature toggle --name ntk-longctx-prefetch --off
```

maria: applying patch to routing now. applying to 3 nodes in canary then progressively. will post logs.

eric: oncall handoff to sasha in 15m if the canary looks good.

(4 minutes later)

maria: Canary applied to nodes db-20..22. kv_insert_rate down ~70% on canary nodes, batch_size median down to 8. no 500s observed on canary.

eric: good sign. proceed to rollout to remainder but pause if any node hit >2x baseline evictions.

kai: rolling full config now. also adding temporary routing policy: route longctx traffic to fallback-quantized variant when queue depth > 150.

(25 minutes later)

sasha: full rollout complete. global kv_insert_rate back to expected bounds. tail latencies reduced to ~1.1x baseline. a few customers with heavy very-long contexts still see slight degradation, but within SLO.

eric: was there any data loss or corruption?

maria: no corruption. a single node rebooted during mitigation but recovered and rejoined. we replayed missing metrics. no persisted model state touched.

devops-bot: collected artifacts:
- `kv-metrics-1958765432.log` (kv_insert/evict histograms)
- `batch-config-diff-1958765432.patch` (the applied change)
- `canary-rolling.log`
links: https://artifacts.internal/r/1958765432/kvmetrics, https://artifacts.internal/r/1958765432/patch

eric: good. escalation avoided. will write a short postmortem and action items. immediate items:
- revert NTK longctx prefetch tuning and re-evaluate with synthetic tests (owner: research/ai infra)
- create throttling guard in router for batch_size > 16 (owner: eng-runtime)
- better alerting: detect continuous-batch size anomalies earlier (owner: eng-sre)

sasha: noted. I'll own the router throttling guard. starting a follow-up ticket.

oncall-bot: Handoff: eric -> sasha. handoff time: 1958770200. summary: mitigations applied, monitoring in steady state.

eric: thanks all. filing incident ticket with attached logs. :thumbsup:

maria: tl;dr — root cause: NTK-prefetch + sliding-window prefetch increased kv churn for very long-context requests, continuous batching aggregated larger batches causing kv blowups; fix: rollback NTK knob + reduce batch window + routing fallback.

sasha: closing pager but keeping watch for 6h. will follow up with postmortem draft.
